redirects.comment: Browsers ask for /favicon.ico whether or not the page declares an icon link. Without a file there, the catch-all SPA rewrite below answers with index.html — a 200 of text/html where an image was expected, which renders as no icon at all rather than as an error anyone would notice. Redirecting to the real PNG is better than shipping a duplicate .ico: one file stays the source of truth, and it is served with the correct image/png rather than a mislabelled payload that X-Content-Type-Options would then refuse.

headers.comment: Security headers. Firebase Hosting sends only HSTS on its own, so without this block the app ships with no clickjacking, MIME-sniffing or referrer protection at all. The CSP was verified by serving this exact static export behind this exact policy and driving it in a browser: the app rendered and hydrated, both service workers registered, and every origin the app needs answered over the network while a control request to example.com was refused by name. Notes on the awkward parts: 'unsafe-inline' in script-src is forced by Next's static export, which inlines its bootstrap and hydration payload with no nonce — the directive still pins WHICH external hosts may serve script, which is the half that stops an injected <script src>. gstatic must be in script-src because /firebase-messaging-sw.js importScripts the Firebase SDK from there, and a worker is governed by the CSP on its own response, not the page's. googleapis.com stays a wildcard on purpose: the probe ran from a logged-out page, so enumerating the six hosts it happened to touch would risk breaking a signed-in path nobody could test, and every host under it is Google-operated anyway. Note wss: is listed SEPARATELY from https: for both googleapis and firebaseio — CSP treats them as different schemes, and a first pass that only tested fetch() missed that Firestore's WebChannel can run over a WebSocket, which fails as a stalled listener rather than as a visible error. firebasestorage.app is listed in its own right because this project's bucket is app-from-ai.firebasestorage.app, the newer bucket domain, which is not under googleapis.com. COOP is same-origin-allow-popups, not same-origin: Google sign-in uses signInWithPopup and the stricter value severs the handle to the popup.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://www.gstatic.com https://apis.google.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com https://*.firebasestorage.app https://*.googleusercontent.com; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https://*.googleapis.com wss://*.googleapis.com https://*.firebaseio.com wss://*.firebaseio.com https://*.firebasestorage.app https://app-from-ai.firebaseapp.com https://api.telegram.org; frame-src 'self' https://app-from-ai.firebaseapp.com https://accounts.google.com https://apis.google.com; worker-src 'self'; manifest-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
